describes: The Holm tip's rock kit (part.py): rigid parts, each one or more convex bodies cut by the tip's own planes (its foliation, joints and sheeting, from the fixture) and turned only as the site turns them, so every piece's planes run with the outcrop's. A plane is [dip, dipToward] in degrees (site frame: x east, y north, z up) or a fixture family's name, at `at` metres from the part's centre along its normal; a facet folds its face back by `tilt` degrees beyond a line `fold` metres from the face's centre, along the direction `dir` degrees in the face (0 along its strike, 90 up its dip), so no face is one flat panel. Each face wears by its kind (`wear`, metres of the round on its edges: the larger of the two faces' at an edge, but a face of an `own` kind, freshly plucked or parted along the foliation, keeps its own crisp edge; never more than capShare of the part's least width), as the first lane's WEAR table and the fixture's chamfers. Levels and budgets are the street's (street.json): a square metre of rock may cost what a square metre of house does.

page.describes: As the street's page: one page a placed piece, charts at the most pixels a metre between pxPerM on the smallest of `sizes` (powers of two, which Unity compresses) that holds them at holdPxPerM; a face that looks down takes `down` of it.

materials.describes: The rock in p3's painted finish: p3's stone (finish.json painted.materials.stone: its wet margin, gloss and brush) at the phyllite's value, its weathered skin between the grey-green and the graphite of docs/stone.md, darker than the house's dressed stone; its colour [C, h] the phyllite's grey-green, as the stone's is its blue-grey; the gneiss's a neutral grey a shade warm, as 58's boulders (no blue: in overcast its coolness is the sky's and it sits below 107's white paint), its warmth in sun the light's.

gneiss._: an erratic's foreign gneiss (a mass's `material`): a mid grey, its weathered skin a little below the plinth's split stone (finish.json stone 51.9) and clearly below white paint in the same light, lighter than the phyllite, its stain the lichen's (paint.py `skin.lichen`: small pale grey-green rosettes, a little lighter than the stone), matte; no brush, its planes one value each

skin.describes: A rock's page (paint.py), its own and not the house plinth's, painted as ref 58 paints its boulders: the light gives each plane its value, and weathering holds 58's three (the top palest, the sides mid, the under-planes darkest). A calm base of the material's value under one broad soft variation (`broad`: ±L* over cells `cellM`); the turf's damp a little darker over the foot (`foot`: L* at the turf, gone `m` up; no wet band, since no eave splashes a rock); the weathered top a little paler, bleached and rain-washed (`top`: L* on faces looking up, from `up`[0] to full at `up`[1]); the under-planes darker, unwashed, the turf's damp and splash reaching them (`under`: L* on faces looking down, from `up`[0] to full at `up`[1]); the top's stipple as 58 paints it (`dabs`), soft painted dabs, not a grain: on a seeded lattice of cells `cellM`, at most one in a cell, `rM` across its radius (skewed small by `skew`), its edge soft over `soft` of it and its outline broken by `warp` of its radius, lighter by `light`.L (a `light` share of them) or darker by `dark`.L, overlapping dabs adding up to `most` times that, a cell holding one with the chance `share` times its density: full on the top, fading down over the shoulders (from `up`[0] to full at `up`[1]), gathered in loose drifts (`drift`: k from k[0] to k[1] over cells `cellM`), thicker toward the weather (`sculpt.chamfer.weather`'s bearing; `weather`: 1 plus as much times a texel's place from the lee side, -1, to the weather side, 1); none in a break's scar nor on the fresh face; the weathering runs as 58's brushwork (`runs`): the water the top sheds leaves many narrow, broken streaks a little darker down the old sides, never one broad band (one read as a smear or a shadow stripe): where it sheds, `perM` places a metre of a side's width (at least one), a few gather (`streaks`, within `spreadM` of the place, at least `gapM` apart), gaps between the places; each starts `startM` under the side's upper edge, under the top's lip, fading in over `headM` (a cut head or break made a short piece a dark square), `widthM` wide, faded to half at `lenM` (finish paint.py's `run`), broken along its length (`broken`: kept where a noise over `breakM` passes from [0] to [1]), wandering `wanderM`, at most `L` darker, on faces looking up less than `up`[1] (full under `up`[0]) and not under past `under`; the breaks (`breaks`, sculpt.py's planes): the scar `L` paler, its weathered skin knocked off, clean of lichen and speckle, and its outline caught by the light in a lip `lipM` wide (`lipL`), as the fresh face's arrises are (`freshLipM` wide), where the stone is open (the occlusion from `ao`[0] to full at `ao`[1]); the contact shade (finish.json `contact`); its cavities dark by the cavity bake (`cavity`: L* where the cavity falls between `cav`). A crack drawn as Hertervig draws one (`crack`): the `set` joint's trace across the biggest side facing the mass's front (its facing at least `front`), at a seeded offset of up to `offset` of the face's span from its middle, carried over onto the next face up its upper end runs into (within `near` metres) for `faces` faces (0: none), drawn on those faces only so it ends where the planes change: a dark line `widthM` wide (`L`) with a lighter lip `lipM` wide on one side (`lipL`), wandering `wander` [metres, amplitude]. The lichen as the material's stain (`lichen`), as crustose lichen grows on coastal gneiss: a population of small round rosettes, pale grey-green, `rM` across their radius (skewed small by `skew`), `count` of them about a middle on the top's weather side (the mean of the up-facing texels' `weather` share furthest toward it), thinning out over `spreadM`; each on an old face looking up at least `up`, at least `clearM` plus its radius in from where the stone turns steeper, never in a scar; two either stand `gapM` apart or merge, overlapping at least `overlap` of their radii: at most `merge` pairs, never three, never a shape wider than `mostM` (one lobed crust read as a stain or a paw print, two side by side as eyes); each margin lobed a little (`lobe`: [cell, amplitude] metres); at most `tries` draws a rosette; none on a face looking down past `under`.

beside.describes: A part judged alone beside the house (LT1HolmTip): the street's house as the street draws it (`gen` and `paint`: the build and page its Street scene holds), each part at `at` in the house's frame (x along its front, y back from it, z up), unturned; the street's street stop as it is, and its eye view the street's, standing off the first part as the street's stands off the house's middle, its height and lens unchanged (`eye`: `from` the first part, looking along `look`); `back` the same eye on the far side (bearing 235, the eye mirrored across the part's front), where the boulder's fresh face is; `high` the view from 12 m over the ground, on the eye's bearing off the first part and looking down at it (`from`, `look`, `fov`); `iso` the near-isometric view of the first part, from bearing 150 about 35° up, a long lens; the boulder is seen from its designed front (bearing 125, the mass's `front`), so it stands south-east of 107's front, 107 beyond it for scale.

tip.describes: The tip's grey-box for the target frame (tip.py, LT1HolmTip -tipGrey): blockin.py's masses from fixtures/lt1-holm-tip.json, with 107 standing where `stand` stands, drawn in grey from the street's street stop.

views.describes: The target frame's own views of the tip, in site metres (x east, y north, z over mean sea level; tip.py moves them into 107's frame for LT1HolmTip): `fov` vertical, `level` the house's level drawn. The low sun is the site's own (blender/parts/rock/views.json lowsun: October, 16:00, from the south-west), not the street's.

water.says: low on the water off the north-west shore (t03, chosen by squint over a view from the north and one from the north point): the shore's blocks step down along it to their lips, the big back rises on the diagonal to 107 on the skyline at the right third, the far shore beyond on the left; the office stands just past the frame's right, the low sun from the right

plan.describes: The target's form plan over the grey-box (tip.py --plan): each face of the tip's blocks (outcrop.py, as blockin.py builds them) takes the zone its kind, height and facing put it in, coloured, with lines at their true spacing: the foliation's trace across the ledged faces that cut it (the lee's and the joints'), and the sheeting's steps on the plucked lee; the ice's backs are left plain, smooth. The storm-wash zone reaches the storm top of `tip.grey` bands at the side's exposure; a riser faces down-ice within `leeFacing` degrees of the ice's way.

storm.says: storm-wash: rounded by the swell, rounds 0.5-1 m; to 2.7 m over mean sea level on the north, 1.0 m on the south (tip.grey bands)

ice.says: ice-planed backs: smooth whalebacks; worn edges 0.04-0.1 m, open joints rounded 0.5-1.3 m

lee.says: plucked lee (ice to 205): crisp steps, risers 0.45-0.9 m (lines 0.6 m), treads 1.6-3.6 m

foliation.says: foliation faces (dip 68 toward 250): stacked ledges 0.1-0.6 m thick; laminae in the bake

joint.says: joint faces J1-J3: crisp, 1.6-3.6 m apart; the foliation's trace across them

made.says: made: the 1862 plinth, the 1882 landing and path cut

grey.describes: The grey frame's values and the rock's shore bands (blockin.py build, rock_mesh). Each block's faces are split at level lines by its side's exposure e (outcrop.py exposure): wet rock and the black lichen band up to `wetTopM` [a, b] = a + b e over mean sea level (the sea note's black band: north +1.2, east +0.55, south +0.45 m); the storm-wash up to the storm top, MHWS (the fixture's spring range halved) + `surgeM` + `runupM` e (docs/research/sea-at-the-shore.md, 3: the annual storm's still water and run-up); turf and heath from `soilM` over the storm top, in a hollow: a block plucked or stripped at least `soilDropM` under the ground's envelope, whose tread lies within `soilSlope` degrees of level and whose side's exposure is at most `soilExposure` (the sheltered, landward side); the ice-bare crest, the lee's upper steps and the sea's side left bare. `values`: each material's [L, roughness]; the rock's tops the lightest, the turf a darker mid, the wet band dark and glossy (wet phyllite darkens only 20-30 %: its gloss carries it), the sea darker than the sky near the shore, the office's walls near 107's.

bands.fetch: The Roads only (runupM 1.9 m; 3.3 m would need the fjord's 10 km): the Roads open north between Battery Head, 0.3-0.75 km north-west of the tip, and Bridge Island to the north-east, with Gull Island 0.3-0.5 km north-north-west and the Teeth and the Pip in them (blender/blockouts/centre_land.py ISLANDS and the areas' map; docs/town-plan.md, The land and 2); the fixture's sea gives about 3 km of fetch to the north, and the west face looks across the west cove to Ferry Point 0.3-0.4 km off. Decided 29 October from the map, closing the sea note's open fact.

shore.describes: The shore block (shore.py): the tip's rock where the sea works it, a fitted part made from its causes: rigid pieces cut along its joints, each set and rounded by its place, none bent. Its place is a record (`lone`: the block judged alone): the waterline's point `at` (site metres), the sea's bearing `face`, its `width` along the shore and `depth` back to the joint behind it, the ice-planed surface's height at its `back` and its `lip`, that surface's slope at the back `backSlope` and its fall across `across` (metres at a metre off its middle, squared). Its outline stands on the joints that most nearly face each way, turned up to `sideTurn` degrees. The foliation cuts it into ribs `leafM` wide toward the sea (most thin: a draw's power `leafSkew`), and J1 cuts each rib across `treadM` apart: a main joint runs on through a rib `through` of the time, jogging up to `jogM`, a rib takes one more between two mains `extra` of the time, each turned up to `riserTurn` degrees. Pieces under `minCell` m² or `minWidthM` across join their longest neighbour. Each trace longer than `bendM` bends at one or two points by up to `bend` of its length, and each inner corner moves up to `wiggleM` (corners nearer than `mergeM` are one). Each piece is sheared down the foliation's dip, so its sides on the partings are the foliation itself and its others stand near upright, its sea side leaning back `riserLean` degrees (at the lip `lipLean`; a plucked piece's not), with a crack between it and its neighbour `crackM` wide (a parting's `fol`, a joint's `joint`, `wash` times wider under the storm top). Its top: above the storm top, the ice's surface, lower by up to `capDrop` at each crack; under it, a ledge the sea left between two main joints, its seaward edge on the ice's surface at the next main joint (the lip's at the front) less up to `washDrop`, dipping `treadDip` degrees toward the sea, so the ledges run on along the shore across the ribs. Each rib stands `lee.stepM` lower than its stoss neighbour; on the lee's ribs a piece was plucked out `lee.share` of the time (the lee rib first), its floor a fresh face `lee.depthM` under its tread, dipping `lee.dip` toward the lee, never under `floor`. Rounds by place, metres: a top edge over a step under `crackDropM` is a crack, left sharp; `crisp` on the lee and in plucked pockets; `sea` on a seaward edge under the storm top (larger the lower and the more exposed); `ice` on the cap and the stoss side; else `joint`; none above `dropShare` of its step or `reachShare` of its top's inner radius. The rounds at or over `bigM` take the level's segments, the rest one. An outline side stands `rowDropM` over its row neighbour's joint. Each piece's foot stands `buryM` under its lowest neighbour's top (the sea's at the lip), never under `base`.

lone.describes: One shore block in grey (tip.py --lone), on the north-west shore where the water frame's near rock stands, with `row` neighbours a side of the same making across joints `gapM` wide (shore.py row), so its sides read as joints and not as a crate's, its views in site metres as tip.views': at eye level from the next block along the shore, from 12 m up, and from the water as the frame sees it.

carve.describes: t04's arm A (carve.py): the shore block made as studios make natural rock, a high body carved from shore.py's pieces at three scales by place (chips off the lee's arrises, the swell's round, the foliation's sheets and their plucked stretches), baked onto a game mesh of the near level's triangles per square metre; arm B the same bake from a downloaded scan's form (`scan`).

game.describes: trisPerM2 a square metre of the block's plan, the cell model's near level (1250 on the lone block)

scan.source: Poly Haven coast_rocks_05 (Rob Tuytel, CC0), its form only

whaleback.describes: The shore block as the ice left it (whaleback.py), the big form first: one smooth hull in the ice's frame (fixture rock.ice), over a superellipse plan a round cap out to `cap` of the way down, then straight slabs, `crestM` over the datum at `crestAt` (metres down-ice and seaward of the block's middle), reaching the datum `stossM` up-ice, `leeM` down-ice, `seaM` seaward and `landM` landward (the plan's exponent `plan`), under `waves` long flutes along the ice's way (their crests within `acrossDeg` of it) `lambdaM` apart and `share` of that high, its foot at `footM`, on a grid `cellM`; the crest at the record's back (`shore.lone.back`). Then cut on the rock's own planes, never smoothed: the back's `sheets`, the ice having planed across the foliation: sheets of skewed thickness (spreads are [mean, shape, least, most], a gamma's few big and many small; `thick` takes the fixture's foliation spacing as its mean) parted along the strike by J1 joints at the fixture's spacing, each edge offset across every joint by up to `jogM` and ending at one `end` of the time (the two sheets one beyond it); in each sheet between two joints everything above one planar tread fitted under the hull above the wet line (`fitM` apart, at least `fewest` points), rising toward the dip by its own `rise`, so an edge crops out as a riser on the foliation, steps over at the joints and dies out where the rise is small, bodies overlapping `overlapM`; along each edge `bites`, every `gapM`, `chance` of the time, a leaf `deep` thick and `long` long between two J1 joints plucked from the higher sheet's edge down to `dropM` under the lower sheet's tread; `cracks`, the main joints across the back, each its family's plane through a point (`at`, metres down-ice and seaward of the crest), `crackM` wide and straight-sided, their `lips` chipped: from `reachM` either side of the crack's point, every `gapM`, `chance` of the time, a wedge off one edge on a plane from the surface `inM` back to the wall `downM` under it, `longM` long between two joints of the family `endOn` names; the lee stepping down-ice from `lee.startM` past the crest, each step's front `spacing` further, across three strips between J1 joints that run on through every step (the main one, and one `landM` toward the land): a J2 face in the sea strip, the foliation's riser in the middle, a J3 face in the land strip, each strip stepping down on its own from up to `jogM` further or nearer, each step's tread `rise` under the last (a few tall faces, many low) on the sheeting dipping `treadDip` degrees down-ice, its own, until under `underM` (at most `most`); at a riser's foot a leaf `leafM` thick plucked out `pluck` of the time, between minor J1 joints `pocketM` apart, `pocketDepthM` under the tread. Edges sharper than `sharpDeg` shade crisp.

slab-block.describes: A joint-bounded block at the tip's north-west waterline, the water frame's foreground (kit.json tip.views water): a low back the ice planed, rising out of the sea toward the land (its top dips 16 degrees toward the sea and runs on under the ground there), rounded over by the swell at its seaward edges and falling away to the west, its most exposed side; its leaves of phyllite stand on edge along the foliation (68 degrees toward 250), flush on its top where the ice planed across them (their traces in the bake), on the ice's lee as steps each packet plucked to its own length along J3, the shorter the further west, so each step bares a leaf's upper face, never its overhang, and at the sea where the two westernmost leaves broke back on fresh J1 faces, the outer the further.

plates.describes: The block parted along its foliation into leaves (phyllite's thin beds, 0.1-0.6 m), from fol-b's side to fol-a's, `t` metres thick (they fill the block); each leaf's faces stand `shift` metres proud (+) or back (-) of the block's: the swell's ramp (`sea`, `north`) and the ice's top are one envelope across all of them, the leaves only ribbing it by a few centimetres where their beds wore unevenly; on the lee each packet plucked to its own length along J3. A plate's own fresh breaks (`breaks`, a list a plate) cut it on planes of its own, crisp: the swell and the frost broke the westernmost leaves back along J1 and the outer one's top along a plane leaning west, and the easternmost along J3, never as an offset copy of the envelope. A leaf's own foliation faces wear as `parting`.

scan.describes: t13 (scan.py): the shore block as one whole scanned roche moutonnee, rigid. `source` the scan (downloaded data: read with --factory-startup only); levelled by the plane of its own open rim; `iceToward` the ice's bearing in that levelled frame (before the turn), read from its form: the abraded stoss faces 90-180 there (smooth, 31-36 degrees), the plucked lee 240-330 (roughness 2-7 times the stoss's, steepest 300-330), the crest at the lee end, the sharpest lee drop along 305-315; turned so it runs the fixture's ice (rock.ice.toward); scaled uniformly so its crest stands at shore.lone.back with its scanned ground `groundM` under the sea, its crest at `crestAt` (t09's, site metres) moved `landwardM` across the ice toward the land, so its seaward waterline lies on t09's (it is twice t09's width across the ice; the rest goes landward); its own pinholes of at most `holeSides` edges closed; its skirt trimmed: the rock is the heightfield's cells connected to the crest above `trimM` over the sea. `land`: the fixture's landform (outcrop.Landform smooth) over `landRegion` [x0, x1, y0, y1], `landBelowM` under it, drawn `landRGB` (linear) beyond `landClearM` of the crest in `landViews` only, as the frame's back and 107's ground (the outcrop round the block is not built); 107 shown there only. The views are t09's, the 12 m and lee ones moved landward with the scan, 12 m's lens `fov12` to hold it whole; t09 is drawn from the same cameras.
scan.credit: Llyn Idwal by megalitharchive, licensed under Creative Commons Attribution

design.describes: r01 (design.py): the shore block designed as a sculptor would, the houses' way (Øystein, 30 October: 'It has to look truly ours'; a stylised world, nothing downloaded in it). The record's facts constrain it (the crest at shore.lone.back over `crestAt`, t09's; the ice's way, fixture rock.ice; the seaward waterline t09's; 107 where it stands); they do not generate it. The ice's back is drawn as section lines (`sections`: for each facing, a bearing, the profile out from the crest as [metres out, height] points, each segment one plane of kind `ice`, named section.index; `*` in a piece is all of them, `*s` one section's), long and gentle up the stoss, arched across; the other planes are drawn by eye, each [facing bearing, slope from level, through [out along the ice, out landward, height] from the crest, kind], the steep ones on the record's sets (fixture rock: J1 the flanks' walls, J2 and J3 the plucked lee's risers, foliation the sea flank's steps). A piece of the `back` is the planes it lists, the rock where each is below; `J<` is the near side of joint J (kind `joint`, its fifth value the gap) and `J>` the far side, so a joint is a real gap; `~p` the far side of p, 4 cm into it, so blocks meet. A piece with `steps` is cut by the foliation's planes (`face`, `slope`, through each `at`), the rock beyond each standing `dropM` lower on the `drops` planes only: broad soft-edged ridges running diagonally down the sea flank. `lee`: the plucked lee in a few big blocks, each its tread, its riser (named by the block's id for the next), its `sides` and the back's planes it lists, `p@dz` lowered dz, its arrises `soft` times the back's. Arrises softened by `bevel`: an edge's width `widthM` times the geometric mean of its two faces' weights by kind (the ice's planes worn most, the foliation's steps less, the joints and plucked risers crispest; a lee block's `soft` scales them), none at the foot (`footM`); the whole moved up or down so its crest is `crestM`, the record's. `stones`: a few loose blocks at the foot by eye ([out along the ice, out landward], size m), each a convex hull of `stonePoints` seeded points, its edges softened `stoneBevel` of its size. The ground: the record's landform lowered `lowerM` within `lowerNearM` of the crest, back by `lowerFarM` (the outcrop round the block is not built: a stand-in for its frame). Soil and turf from the record's shore bands (tip.grey bands: storm top MHWS + surgeM + runupM e, soil soilM over it) read by each face's own facing (fixture sea.exposure between its four sides): the record reads them by the outcrop's side, which puts this block's whole height in the storm wash. The turf a mat `turfM` thick, its edge rolled over in a quarter round `lipM` wide, the till under its edge a cut bank `bankSteep` times its slope for `bankM`. Tufts are the pack's (tufts.py, unchanged): a fringe along the lip, the heath habitat on the mat within `heathWithinM`, and in the joints' gaps and along the foot of each lee riser above the soil line. Views: t09's lone views (`fov12` for 12 m), the lee view `lee` [bearing, out, up] from the 12 m view's target, the tip's water frame.

body.describes: r02 (body.py): the shore block as designed signed-distance bodies, silhouette first. In the ice's frame (s down the ice, toward rock.ice.toward; t across it, toward the land; metres from `crestAt`, z over mean sea level). `section` is the long section along the crest line [s, z], drawn from the record (crest at its back, the ice's way, t09's seaward waterline) and the t13 study's measured proportions (stoss 6.8 m to the crest at 23 degrees, crest 73% along, the lee's drop 66 degrees, width 1.46 times the length; numbers only, nothing taken from the scan's geometry), pushed: an arched back, the crest 73% along, no flat top; `crestLine` the crest's offset across the ice at stations s, so the back sweeps; `half` the plan's half widths toward the sea and the land at stations s; `cross` the cross section's power each side, the sea flank fuller and steeper. A plane is [facing, slope, [s, t, z], kind]; `joints` names the record's joints, each a gap `gapM` wide, and a face written "J" or "~J" is that joint's near or far side (never hand-write a joint's far side: [b+180, slope] is its mirror, not its parallel, and leaves a sliver). `blocks`: each block is the back on one `side` of a joint, then its `cuts` (planes), its `split` (a joint, from `fromS` down the ice) and its `pluck` (convex pieces taken out, each the union of the body cut by each of its faces, so corners inside it stay crisp): big low, small high in the lee. Every cut is joined by a rolling-ball round of its kind's radius (`round`, metres), so planes meeting gently keep their flats. Meshed by openvdb at `fineM` in a narrow band (`bandM`) round a coarse grid; faces more than `trimM` under the ground dropped; then the near level's budget by surface (street.json) and face-weighted normals. `spike` is the splinter check (Øystein, 30 Oct: no sharp pointy things): at each surface voxel the share of a cube of half width `ballM` that is rock (a flat 0.5, a square edge 0.25, a square corner 0.125); under `least` above `aboveM` is a spike. `ground`: the record's smooth landform lowered round the block, `lowerLeeM` in the lee's hollow down-ice of `leeFromS` and `lowerFlankM` on the land flank, fading from `nearM` to `farM` of the crest. `view12` the 12 m view's lens and target; `leeView` [bearing, distance, height] of the lee view; `grey` the grey check's values; `silhouette` the step 1 flats' values.

mass.describes: r03 (mass.py): the outcrop as a few rigid masses, ref 57's LOW ROCKY OUTCROP the bar (its ROUNDED and JAGGED BOULDER the range of edges). Each mass is convex, authored in site bearings (x east, y north, z up from its base; bearings 0 = north) so every mass shares the record's structure: its big planes on the record's joint sets (J1 135/315, J2 45/225, J3 352/172, the foliation 250 at 68), the worn faces free. `tops` its top facets [facing, slope, [x, y, z], kind]; `sides` [facing, slope, dist, kind], a plane through dist metres toward `facing` at its base; `chips` authored breaks; `sinkM` how deep a mass stands in the turf; `tilt` [toward, degrees] an erratic's lean, its tops, sides and own structure turned rigidly about its middle at the turf so its top tips toward `toward` (mass.py `lean`), as the ground it settled in explains. Then the wear rule (`wear`, seeded by the mass): on each arris where a face of an `exposed` kind meets another, from each end at `arris.share` a broad facet starting `arris.fromEnd` of the way along and deepening to `arris.depthM` at the corner (sizes skewed: a few big, many small, `skew` the power); at each corner of three faces at `corner.share` a facet `corner.depthM` deep, its facing the corner's mean turned up to `jitterDeg`; worn where an exposed face meets, else a crisp chip. Every face bulges out (`bulge`): a dome over the face standing `share` of its size by its kind times `amp`, its crown shifted up to `shift`, reaching `reach` times its size. Then the mass is split into rigid blocks (`fracture`): the record's joints, foliation and sheeting (orientation and spacing from `record`) shown at `show` of each set, each plane splitting the one block a seeded point on it lies in, never leaving a block under `leastM` across, at most `most`; a seam is its family's tight width (the record's outcrop `tightM`), opening `widen` a metre up; each block settles by a seeded turn of `settleDeg` about its foot (a lean, claiming no history). Every arris is a rolling-ball round of the smaller of its two faces' kinds (`round`, metres; cut in order of falling radius), varied along it (`vary`: by height in the mass from exposure[0] at its base to [1] at its top, and seeded waves of `wave` share over `waveM`), and never more than the record's `capShare` of its block's least width but for the `capExempt` kinds. Masses and blocks are only moved and turned into place, never bent. `flat` the flat-share check: mesh within `flat.M` of a face's plane and `flat.deg` of its facing; `spike` the splinter check (body's measure). `judge` the step 1 view, matched to 57's boulder row: the camera `elev` degrees over the mass's middle, `fov`, `fit` times its size off, at each mass's `front` bearing and `back` degrees round from it; the sun `sunRel` degrees from the camera's bearing (minus is to the camera's right), `sunEl` high, warm; a blue sky.

spall: frost spalled a flake off its south-east top corner a few winters ago, the scar still crisp

structure._: its own, not the bedrock's: a gneiss banded a few centimetres thick, and the joint set the frost broke its south-west face off along (the plucked face is one), opening again behind it

masses.says: an erratic of foreign gneiss from the moraine, about 2.7 by 1.9 m and 1.2 m out of the turf: transport rounded it into a broad top on steep sides that tuck in at the turf (board 17, 19, 26, 56), and frost broke one fresh face off its south-west side (crisp, board 15); its own foliation, not the bedrock's; it sank into the soft till about a sixth of its height, its heavier north end deeper (`tilt`), so the turf banks higher on its south side
the high back, 57's crown: a broad low dome of planes, polished toward the ice's source, worn noses to the stoss and both flanks, the lee plucked on J2 and J3
57's middle front slab: a thick sheet dipping gently to the sea, its front a steep worn face under a soft arris, J1 ends, its back on J2 tucked under the crown
57's jagged boulder as a plucked lee block: a near-level tread with crisp plucked arrises on J2 and J3, the foliation a big sloping face, the stoss shoulder worn back toward the crest

sculpt.describes: Stage 2, the high-poly sculpt (sculpt.py): the blockout's designed planes as one form, every plane kept flat (no bulge, no grain, nothing smoothed over a face), each arris worn back `chamfer` metres into its two faces square to it: `big` where its bisector faces the weather (toward `weather`, [bearing, degrees over the horizon]: the tip's sea and its wind, over `at` of the bisector's facing), `small` where it is sheltered, `fresh` where a fresh face meets; a worn arris a true round (a cylinder tangent to both faces, so it shades from one plane's normal to the other's; 58's planes meet decisively, so rounds stay 2-5 cm), its width changing end to end by a seeded share of `taper`, a fresh one a single crisp facet; its creases crisp to `soft`. Then a few cracks cut as clean V-grooves on the mass's own joint planes (`crack`), a few corners chipped off by planar cuts (`chip`), each a plane held to its own corner (a plane that would run more than `reach` times its depth from the corner is not cut), and a few breaks knocked off arrises as a planar floor and step (`breaks`, ref 59's notches: the top corner the mass's record says frost spalled (`spall`), a few along the fresh face's arrises, one on the front's level foot arris, each a floor biting `biteM` [upper, lower] into its two faces so it faces the sky and lights, running out down the arris, and a step 25-35 degrees off square whose underside goes dark (a square one bakes as a beaded line); concave, so in the high-poly alone, carried by the bake). `leastArrisM` the shortest arris the designed planes may leave out of the turf: shorter is a pinch, and sculpt.py stops. Sizes in metres, skewed to the small end by `skew`.

game.describes: Stage 3, the game mesh (game.py): the sculpt's form without its fine marks meshed at `voxelM`, cut `underM` under the turf, decimated to `fill` of each level's budget (street.json's by surface); the high-poly's arris (Col R) its smooth form's mean curvature between `arris` (1/m), by differences `curveM` apart; the bake's cage and reach a level (`rays`, metres); the levels' normals by the designed planes (a face within `flatDeg` of its plane is that plane's, the rest the chamfers' turn; every edge between two planes or a plane and a chamfer hard, and a plane's faces take its own normal, so each plane shades flat and the chamfers alone turn).

foot.describes: A mass's till stones (foot.py), the grass round them being the ground's (ground.py). The turf line is the sculpted form's outline at the turf (game.py's cut), read on `rays` bearings round it, its drip line the form's widest reach up to `dripM` over it; broken by stretches where it shows (seeded noise over `gapM` of the line, `gap` of it), where a stone lies. The stones (`stones`): `count`, `sizeM` across (skewed small by `skew`), flattened to `flat` of it, each a hull of `points` seeded points chamfered by `chamfer` of its size (a few facets, as the boulder), sunk `sink` of its height, within `withinM` of the turf line, where it breaks if one of `tries` seeded bearings finds a gap; `dL` below the boulder's, as 58's fallen pieces: few, darker, a little angular, sunk deep. Their colour their own (`paint` [C, h]: a grey the turf's soil has stained, never the boulder's blue; L, C, h varied by `vary`), with the skin's foot rule over the stone's own height and their own top rule (`topL` for `skin.top`'s L: 0, no pale top).

ground.describes: Stage 6, the ground (ground.py): the pack's `community` (growth.json habitats, its `season`'s colours where a species has them) over `box` (the scene's frame, x east, y north; the stand-in floor's extent), as the growth's tufts, and under them its map (growth.ground_map) at `px`; no tuft in the house (its near level's foot: edges below `house`[0] m on a `house`[1] m grid, grown by `house`[2] m) or within `clearM` of a part's turf line or within `stoneClear` of a till stone's radius (so its own top shows over the bank). Drawn by GrowthTufts with `draw` (each level's reach `to` from the eye, crossfaded over `fade` of it; past `thinFrom` m only the ranks under thinFrom over the distance stay, down to `keepMin`, widened by `widen`). The bank against a part (`bank`): the community's own feet give way to the bank's at `perSqm`, over its zone: full from the turf line to the drip line (the form's widest reach up to `dripM` over the turf), easing out over `reachM` past it, times `reachVary` by bearing (seeded noise over `reachWaveM` of the line), times 1 + `shed` of where the stone sheds its rain (its top drained, by bearing) + `lee` of the lee (away from sculpt.chamfer.weather); `mix` its species; taller by `tall` [least, most] between none and full shed and lee, shorter by `exposed` of the weather's side; under an overhang `under` of the density and `underScale` of the size; leaning out from the stone by `leanOut` degrees; a tuft that would enter the stone leans `leanStep` degrees further for `tries` tries, shrinking at each, or is left out. Its ground damper toward `groundDamp`[1] by `groundDamp`[0] where it sheds; its tips toward the species' `damp` colour likewise (the shader).
